test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Sept, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Who is the nominal executive authority of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **President** of India is the nominal executive authority of the country.
 
• The President is considered the **ceremonial head of state**, functioning as the symbol of the **unity, integrity, and solidarity of the nation**.
 
• Although the President of India is vested with considerable powers, these are **exercised on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers**.
 
• The President's role is largely ceremonial with real executive power being vested in the Prime Minister and their council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The office of the President of India was established when the country became a republic on **26th January 1950**.
 
• **Article 52** of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a President of India.
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament, as well as the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The President holds office for a term of** five years** from the date on which they enter upon their office.
 
• In the case of a **vacancy due to death, resignation, or removal**, the **Vice President discharges the duties of the President until a new President is elected**.
